intro: An accumulation function $g(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt$ adds up the signed area under $f$ from $a$ to $x$. Drag $x$ and watch the area build while the graph of $g$ draws itself: where $f$ is positive $g$ climbs, where $f$ is negative it falls, and its slope is always $f(x)$.
howItWorksTitle: How the areas and the graph of g are computed
howItWorks:
For graphs made of segments and semicircles the tool uses the same geometry you would: triangles, trapezoids, rectangles and quarter or half circles, kept exact (an answer like $4 - 2\pi$ is shown that way). For a formula it integrates numerically to many decimal places. The tangent line on the graph of $g$ always has slope $f(x)$: that is the Fundamental Theorem, part 1. Net change shows part 2: the shaded area from one point to another equals the rise of $g$ between them.

  • Signed area. Area below the axis counts negative. When $x$ is less than $a$, $g(x) = -\int_x^a f(t)\,dt$, so the sign flips again.
  • Reading $g$ from $f$. $g$ increases where $f > 0$, has a relative maximum where $f$ changes from positive to negative, and is concave up where $f$ is increasing.
  • In context (Unit 8). The amount in a tank is its starting amount plus the integral of rate in minus rate out.

Test yourself makes new problems from a seed (the problem code). Every key is recomputed independently by the validator, and a wrong answer is matched to the usual slip: unsigned area, a full circle for a half, the wrong lower limit, a dropped initial value, a missing chain-rule factor.
